The galaxy is clearly resolved into three separate clumps and a smooth component (halo; Figures 1(b), (d)).
All components have formed 50% of their stars in the last 300 Myr. All components are also undergoing a simultaneous burst of star formation in the last 150 Myr (bottom-right panels in Figure 1).
The simultaneous burst of star formation in the galaxy components indicate that MACS0416-Y1 is a late-stage merger.
The UV emission is offset from the dust continuum showing dust obscured star formation in the galaxy.
While MACS0416-Y1 is considerably more gas rich compared to the local and cosmic noon galaxies, it has comparable SFR surface density for a given gas mass surface density.
The emission line ratios of the galaxy indicate an evolved interstellar medium similar to z ∼ 2 star-forming galaxies.
Further, we find possible presence of ionization from an active galactic nucleus (AGN) using emission line diagnostics; however, we do not detect a broad-line component in the Hβ emission line.
We find that the measured position of MACS0416-Y1 on the R2-R3 diagram can be described by a shock velocity of >1000 km s −1 .
The central clump is less massive compared to the other clumps and possibly formed in the merging process of the two larger clumps.

All components are also undergoing a simultaneous burst of star formation in the last 150 Myr (bottom-right panels in Figure 1). The simultaneous burst of star formation in the galaxy components indicate that MACS0416-Y1 is a late-stage merger.
Spatially resolved spectroscopy of MACS0416-Y1 is required to study the kinematics of the three resolved clumps to further strengthen the evidence for merger.

We also performed a fit with the nonparametric SFH from K. G. Iyer et al. (2019) to enable a more direct comparison with DENSE BASIS and found similar results to the double power-law SFH.

all_quotes.loc: 2.5. Cold Dust Spectral Energy Distribution Fitting
all_quotes.quote: Given that the lack of data in the far-infrared prevents us from estimating the dust temperature (T dust ), we create models using two free parameters, the dust mass (M dust ) and the dust emissivity index (β), at different fixed T dust .

We note that the molecular gas mass estimated from L[C II ] may be related to star formation and thus SFE (J. Kennicutt 1998). The ongoing star formation burst may lead to an overestimation of the molecular gas mass.

all_quotes.loc: 3.2. Physical Properties with Emission Line Ratios
all_quotes.quote: In the NIRSpec prism data, [O III ]λ4363 is blended with Hγ. We calculate the expected Hγ flux based on the Hβ/ Hδ ratio and subtract the same from the combined [O III ]λ4363+Hγ flux to estimate the [O III ]λ4363 flux.

all_quotes.loc: 3.4. Is MACS0416-Y1 a Possible Active Galactic Nucleus?
all_quotes.quote: Further exploration of the gas kinematics for MACS0416-Y1 and the detection of a broad-line component using higher-resolution spectroscopy are required to make an inference in the existence of an AGN in MACS0416-Y1.
Spatially resolved spectroscopy of MACS0416-Y1 is required to study the kinematics of the three resolved clumps to further strengthen the evidence for merger.
